# Free Lunch Lab

> Free Lunch Lab ("There is such a thing as a free lunch.") is a curated directory of apps and projects that pay you a basic income or rewards just for existing: crypto UBI, passive apps, cashback and more. Every entry links to its official source and has a "last checked" month, and the risks and cautions are listed next to the rewards. The site is available in 7 languages (en, ja, zh, hi, es, de, ar).

- Referral links: some sign-up links are the maintainer's referral links. They are marked in the data (`referral` in services.json) and labelled "Referral link" below; official URLs are always given too.
- License: content is CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), referral links excluded.
- Data last checked: 2026-10
- Short index: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/llms.txt

### Circles (Gnosis App)

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/circles/
- Category: Crypto UBI
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: Web of trust / invites
- Trust check: Cash out: Unverified; Market price: Unverified; Public operator: Yes
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://app.gnosis.io/

A Gnosis project where every person issues their own currency. Circles 2.0 launched in May 2025, and in June 2026 the Gnosis App was rebuilt around Circles. This site has no referral link for it yet

What you get: 1 CRC per hour (24 per day)

What you need: Sign up in the Gnosis App and get invited by an existing Circles member. The inviter pays 96 CRC and the newcomer gets 48 CRC as a welcome bonus

Cautions: You can’t start without a member to invite you. CRC’s market price and ways to cash out are not confirmed. Gnosis has announced plans to spin the Gnosis App out of Gnosis Ltd into a separate company, so details may change

### Mein Grundeinkommen

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/meingrundeinkommen/
- Category: Passive apps
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: No verification, ID document KYC (optional)
- Trust check: Cash out: Yes; Public operator: Yes
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://www.mein-grundeinkommen.de/
- Referral link (maintainer's own referral; not covered by the content license): https://meinbge.de/fuer-dich/4143ce95b90cf10386f4?utm_campaign=freundschaft

A free lottery run by a nonprofit association in Berlin and funded by crowdfunding donations. Draws are held regularly, and each winner gets €1,000 a month for 12 months, no strings attached (real cash, not crypto)

What you get: €1,000 a month for a year if you win

What you need: Register with your email and confirm your participation for each draw. You must be 16 or older, and your name and date of birth must match your ID if you win

Cautions: A 2020 statement from the organisation said anyone can take part regardless of age or where they live, but current rules for people outside Germany and payouts abroad are not confirmed. The site is in German. It's a lottery, so most entrants receive nothing. Winnings may be taxed in your country

### UBI4ALL

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/ubi4all/
- Category: Passive apps
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: No verification, ID document KYC (optional)
- Trust check: Cash out: Yes; Public operator: Yes
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://www.ubi4all.org/

A free raffle run by a European non-profit founded in 2020 (legal entity: “EBI Politische Teilhabe in Europa gemeinnützige UG” in Germany). Each time donations reach €9,600, a basic income worth €9,600 in total is raffled off, no strings attached (real cash, not crypto). The monthly amount and duration depend on the income level of the winner’s country: high-income OECD countries such as Japan get €800 a month for 1 year, low-income countries €160 a month for 5 years. Raffles are held whenever the pot is funded; 10 so far (Oct 2026). The 9th was held live at the BIEN Congress in Brazil in Aug 2025. The team is unpaid. There is no referral link or referral bonus

What you get: €9,600 if you win (in Japan: €800 a month for a year)

What you need: Create a free account on the official site and register for each raffle (there is also an option to confirm for all raffles at once). Monthly donors (“UBI Beavers”, from €1) are entered automatically. You must be 16 or older, your name, date of birth and country must match your ID, and winners are verified with their ID. Eligibility is per the official site (it is open worldwide and lists Japan as an example country, but sign-up from Japan has not yet been tested by this site)

Cautions: It’s a raffle, so the odds are low and depend on how many people take part. Raffles only happen when donations fill the €9,600 pot, so the timing is irregular. Unless you are a UBI Beaver, you have to register for each raffle. Residents of the previous winner’s country are excluded from the next draw. Payouts go to SEPA bank accounts; other methods have their fees taken from the prize. How the prize is taxed depends on your country

### Ğ1 (June)

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/g1/
- Category: Crypto UBI
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: Web of trust / invites
- Trust check: Cash out: With conditions; Market price: Unverified; Public operator: Yes
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://duniter.org/g1/

A libre currency based on the Relative Theory of Money. It runs on the open-source Duniter software, and every member receives newly created Ğ1 each day as a “Universal Dividend”. Launched in March 2017 and moved to Duniter v2 in March 2026. There is no referral link or referral bonus

What you get: Ğ1 every day once you are a member (Universal Dividend)

What you need: Create a wallet and get certified by at least 5 existing members through the Web of Trust. Certifiers are expected to know you in person

Cautions: The community is mostly French-speaking and built on in-person ties, so joining from outside it (e.g. from Japan) is very hard. Non-members can still hold Ğ1 in a wallet but do not receive the daily dividend. Ğ1 is mainly traded for goods and services, and swapping it for regular money is peer-to-peer only

### Palai

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/palai/
- Category: Passive apps
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: Phone number
- Trust check: Cash out: No; Public operator: Unverified
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://palai.org/en
- Referral link (maintainer's own referral; not covered by the content license): https://palai.org/en?referrer=eltociear%2B856536b6d-da3a-4f27-9bcf-8eef2ce05bc2

Its own currency that pays everyone a daily basic income simply for being human. No install and no money to pay in. Idle balances slowly “evaporate” (2.000% a year as of Oct 2026), and that amount is redistributed as basic income. When you invite a friend, you get an extra day’s basic income

What you get: Palai (¶) basic income every day

What you need: Sign up via the referral link and get certified by adding a mobile phone number (no ID needed). You claim your income yourself; days not claimed within 10 days are lost

Cautions: As of Oct 2026 there is no way to cash Palai out into euros or other money and no official exchange rate; you can only trade it for goods and services with people who accept Palai. The site doesn’t name the operator, only that it is “supported by Social Impact Lab Leipzig”

### Dotare

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/dotare/
- Category: Crypto UBI
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: not specified
- Trust check: Cash out: Yes; Market price: Yes; Public operator: Yes
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://dotare.io/

A “global universal basic income” endowment on Cardano. Staking yield on ADA pledged by benefactors grows the fund, and its earnings are paid out monthly in ADA. 2027 beneficiaries get 10 ADA a month for 12 months (the amount can grow as the fund grows). There is no means test. Run by Dotare, LLC in the US. There is no referral link or referral bonus

What you get: 10 ADA a month for a year if you are chosen (2027 cycle)

What you need: Be 18 or older. Sign up on the official site and apply for each year you want to take part. When your turn comes, pass a quick identity check (to show you are human) and set up a Cardano wallet to receive payments

Cautions: For the 2027 cycle, applications closed on 31 Aug 2026 and enrollment closes on 30 Nov 2026; when someone signing up now would start receiving is not confirmed. Payouts go in line order, and as of 24 Oct 2026 the site showed 147 citizens and 2 beneficiaries. ADA’s price swings a lot

### ORO (World App)

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/oro/
- Category: Crypto UBI
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: World ID (Orb)
- Trust check: Cash out: With conditions; Market price: Yes; Public operator: Unverified
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://world.org/ecosystem/app_f1e44837a5e3c2af4da8925b46027645

A mini app inside World App. Billed as “a token every human can claim daily”, it lets you claim ORO on World Chain once a day. World’s listing mentions inviting friends to earn more, but no invite link was found in the app as of Oct 2026. Developed by Grupo de Fiesta, with about 3.9 million users (World’s listing page, Oct 2026)

What you get: ORO tokens every day

What you need: Install World App, prove you are human with World ID (confirmed from Japan with Orb verification), then open the ORO mini app and claim every day

Cautions: The daily amount is not stated on the official pages (a World Chain announcement in Sep 2025 said 1 ORO a day; later reports say it was reduced). Confirmed usable from Japan with an Orb-verified World ID in Oct 2026; whether a lower (non-Orb) verification level is enough is unknown. ORO trades on a decentralized exchange (DEX) with little liquidity, and as of Oct 2026 one ORO is worth well under a cent. No company details for the operator were found

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/axo/
- Category: Crypto UBI

- Region: available in Japan and worldwide

- Referral code (maintainer's own): 932BDA

A mini app inside World App. Claim AXO (AXOLOCOIN), a token on World Chain, once a day with a tap. “Premium” at 1 WLD a month triples your daily claim. It also has a referral system. David Mateos is named as the founder. About 300,000 users (World’s listing page, Oct 2026)

What you get: AXO tokens every day

What you need: Open the mini app in World App via the referral link (referral code 932BDA), prove you are human with World ID (confirmed from Japan with Orb verification), and claim every day

Confirmed usable from Japan with an Orb-verified World ID in Oct 2026; whether a lower (non-Orb) verification level is enough is unknown. AXO can be swapped for WLD on a decentralized exchange (DEX), but as of Oct 2026 liquidity is only about $2,000 and one AXO is worth a tiny fraction of a cent. No operating company details were found

### AI-DAC (World App)

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/aidac/
- Category: Crypto UBI
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: World ID (Orb)
- Trust check: Cash out: With conditions; Market price: Yes; Public operator: Yes
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://lp.ai-dac.com/

A mini app inside World App that calls itself an “AI-powered universal basic income platform”. People verified as human with World ID receive DAC UBI and use it to back autonomous “AI CEOs” that plan, build and ship apps, and to vote and give feedback on releases. Run by founder Kei Iwami. There is no referral link or referral bonus

What you get: UBI in DAC tokens

What you need: Open the AI-DAC mini app in World App and prove you are human with World ID (confirmed from Japan with Orb verification)

Cautions: The amount, frequency, regions and cash-out are not stated officially. Confirmed usable from Japan with an Orb-verified World ID in Oct 2026; whether a lower (non-Orb) verification level is enough is unknown. DAC is an ERC-20 token on World Chain with a stated total supply of 100M, but the contract has no supply cap and the owner can mint and airdrop more at any time, which can dilute its value. The project says it is not for investment and its value is not guaranteed. There is a DAC/WLD pair on a decentralized exchange (DEX), but as of Oct 2026 liquidity is only about $170. App production orders are paid separately in World USDC

### Ubiquitus

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/ubiquitus/
- Category: Passive apps
- Payout: recurring
- Region: US residents only, not available from Japan
- Verification: not specified
- Trust check: Cash out: Yes; Public operator: Yes
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://www.ubiquitus.org/

A US “basic income anyone can join” experiment. Voluntary gifts form a pool invested mainly in stocks (with a small crypto sleeve), and each month 0.5% of it is split equally among all members and paid via Venmo. Giving does not increase your share. Started in 2023 by founder and developer Ryan Frigo. The October 2026 payout was $0.10 each to 266 people. There is no referral link or referral bonus

What you get: A small equal cash share on the 1st of each month (Venmo)

What you need: US residents aged 18+. Verify with a 1¢ Venmo transaction (no ID upload, no means test)

Cautions: As of Oct 2026 it cannot be used from Japan (the terms limit it to US residents; not working from Japan was confirmed first-hand). The per-person amount is tiny, falls with the pool, and payouts are stated to be not guaranteed and able to stop at any time. It describes itself as an informal social experiment, not a company. Recipients must report payments as income

### Gradido

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/gradido/
- Category: Passive apps
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: No verification
- Trust check: Cash out: Unverified; Public operator: Yes
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://gradido.net/en/
- Referral link (maintainer's own referral; not covered by the content license): https://gdd.gradido.net/u/eltociear

A currency system billed as a “natural economy”, named after Gratitude, Dignity and Donation. Money is created by everyone rather than as debt: contributions to the common good earn an “active basic income” of 20 GDD an hour, up to 50 hours (1,000 GDD) a month. Unused money shrinks at 50% a year (about 5.61% a month). Run by Gradido Akademie International, a research and development association in Austria with a branch in Germany

What you get: 20 GDD per hour of common-good work (up to 1,000 GDD a month)

What you need: Create a free Gradido account through the referral link, log your common-good contributions and receive GDD

Cautions: The official FAQ says that for now it is a thank-you point reward system and not a cryptocurrency. There is no official information on exchanging GDD for euros or other money. Confirmed usable from Japan in Oct 2026 (first-hand). If someone who signed up through a referral link later makes a financial contribution to Gradido (such as a donation), the referrer is credited with GDT (Gradido Transform), according to the public wallet source code. There is no bonus just for signing up

### WowApp

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/wowapp/
- Category: Passive apps
- Payout: recurring

### Idena (iDNA)

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/idena/
- Category: Crypto UBI
- Payout: recurring
- Region: available in Japan and worldwide
- Verification: Validation ceremony, Web of trust / invites
- Trust check: Cash out: With conditions; Market price: Yes; Public operator: With conditions
- Last checked: 2026-10
- Official URL: https://www.idena.io/

A proof-of-person blockchain built on “one person, one vote”. You prove you are human in a synchronized “validation ceremony” held worldwide at the same time, by solving picture puzzles called FLIPs. In Oct 2026 ceremonies were held every 5 days, starting at 15:00 UTC. Once validated, you earn iDNA mining rewards in real time while your node runs, plus rewards per session. It is an open-source project; 159 accounts took part in the 24 Oct 2026 ceremony. There is no referral link

What you get: iDNA (mining rewards while your node runs, plus validation rewards)

What you need: Follow the pinned message in the official Telegram to get a free invitation code from a validated member or the Idena team. Join with the web app (a shared node works too) or your own node, and be online at ceremony time to solve FLIPs (confirmed usable from Japan in Oct 2026, first-hand)

Cautions: You must be online at a fixed time (midnight in Japan) or you will not be validated, so it takes effort. The network is very small: iDNA is about $0.0012 (Oct 2026), the market cap is about $120,000, and the only exchange CoinGecko shows is PancakeSwap (BSC), so liquidity is low. Cashing out means selling on an exchange. Invitation codes must not be bought or sold; they are free. If you delegate to someone else’s “pool”, the pool owner can take your stake

A service from Kabu & Peace Inc., whose president and CEO is Yusaku Maezawa. When you pay for KABU& electricity, gas, mobile, fibre internet, Wi-Fi, water, travel, telemedicine and other services, or spend with the KABU& Card, you receive “share vouchers” (kabu hikikaeken). For standard members the rate is 1% for electricity and gas, 5% for mobile, fibre, water and telemedicine, and 1 voucher per ¥200 on the card; paid Plus and Premium memberships raise the rates. During a set offering period you can apply to exchange vouchers for the company’s class shares (KABU& class shares); the 4th offering’s issue price is ¥8 a share (8 vouchers), and its application period is 6–26 Nov 2026. Register as a KABU& member, then contract a service and pay for it. To exchange vouchers for shares you must apply during the offering period, pass ID-based eKYC (driving licence, My Number card, etc.) and open and link a Daiwa Connect Securities account (by 6 Dec 2026 for the 4th offering)

Cautions: The shares are unlisted: right now they cannot be sold or cashed, and their future value and liquidity are uncertain. The official site itself says a listing is not guaranteed, and the value may fall below the issue price. Vouchers basically come only from paying for services, so switching only makes sense if the price and terms of the service itself suit you. Vouchers can be exchanged for shares only during set offering periods, and they expire one year after the end of the month of your latest grant. Check the terms, the prospectus and when vouchers turn into shares before applying. The official referral notes say rewards may be voided if referral codes are spread on social media. KABU& also warns that offers to sell you its shares by phone, social media or email are very likely investment fraud: the shares can only be obtained with vouchers

## Essays

### Universal high income: who pays?

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/universal-high-income/
- Published: 2026-10-29

In November 2023, closing the UK’s AI Safety Summit in conversation with Rishi Sunak, Elon Musk said “there will come a point where no job is needed”, and added: “We won’t have universal basic income, we’ll have universal high income.”[1] Six months later, speaking by video link to VivaTech in Paris, he went further: “Probably none of us will have a job.” AI and robots would provide the goods and services people want, there would be “no shortage of goods or services”, and to make it work there would need to be a “universal high income”. CNN noted that he did not say what that would look like.[2]

As far as the public record goes, that is the whole proposal: a forecast of abundance, plus a name. This essay asks the question the name skips. If the robots do the work, who pays the high income, and through what pipe does it reach people?

#### What the framing gets right

Opinion: Credit where it is due. Most talk about AI and jobs is defensive: retraining, safety nets, how to survive being replaced. Universal high income flips the question from “how do we survive job loss?” to “how do we share abundance?” That is a better question. If machines really make goods and services far cheaper, the problem stops being scarcity and becomes distribution. Basic income advocates have argued for decades that distribution is a political choice, not a law of nature. It is useful to hear the same point from someone who runs AI and robotics companies.

#### The gaps

Opinion: Who pays? Abundance does not distribute itself. In a world where AI earns the money, the profits land with whoever owns the models, the data centres and the robots. Getting them to everyone else needs a mechanism: a tax, a dividend, a public fund, a share register. Musk has not named one. A promise of income with no payer is a forecast, not a policy.

Opinion: Not everything gets cheaper. AI can cut the cost of software, translation and perhaps, one day, manufacturing. It does little for land, which nobody is making more of, or for housing where people want to live. Positional goods, such as the best school, the view or the scarce ticket, are scarce by definition. And care from an actual human may become more valuable, not less, precisely because it is the one thing machines are not. If those prices rise while gadgets get cheap, people can be richer in stuff and still feel poor.

Opinion: “High” is relative. A high income is high compared with someone. If everyone receives the same generous amount, the prices of the scarce things above adjust to it, and what feels high in year one becomes the new floor. The useful question is not “how high?” but “how much of the scarce stuff can it buy?”

Opinion: The people promising it own the AI. That is not a conspiracy, just the shape of the incentive. When the owners of a technology say its benefits will reach everyone, the details of how matter more, not less. A share of profits that depends on the goodwill of the people holding them is a gift, and gifts can stop.

#### Pipes people have actually proposed

Some people have tried to draw the pipe. In “Moore’s Law for Everything” (March 2021), Sam Altman proposed an American Equity Fund, filled by taxing large companies 2.5% of their market value each year, paid in shares, and 2.5% of the value of privately held land, paid in dollars. He estimated that within a decade each of 250 million American adults would get about $13,500 a year.[3] He picked land because its supply is fixed, which is exactly the problem above.

In May 2024, on the All-In podcast, Altman floated “universal basic compute”: everybody gets “a slice of GPT-7’s compute” to use, resell or donate. He did not say how it would work.[4]

The Windfall Clause, from researchers at the Centre for the Governance of AI at Oxford’s Future of Humanity Institute (2020), proposes that AI firms commit in advance to donate a significant share of any extremely large profits that only a transformative AI breakthrough could produce.[5]

There is also a working precedent. Since 1982, Alaska has paid residents an annual dividend from its Permanent Fund, which turns the state’s oil and mineral wealth into a lasting financial resource; the first payment was $1,000 each.[6] (See our timeline (https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/timeline/#tl-alaska).) Swap “oil” for “AI profits” and you have the cleanest real-world template for a high income. There is evidence on what cash does, too. The OpenResearch study gave 1,000 people $1,000 a month for three years. Its 2024 results found that recipients spent more and worked one to two fewer hours a week, with no improvement in job quality.[7] (Timeline entry (https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/timeline/#tl-openresearch).)

#### How crypto UBI answers “who pays”

The apps on this site have had to answer the question for real, at small scale. They answer it in three different ways.

World handed out newly issued tokens. When WLD launched in 2023, 75% of its 10 billion supply was earmarked for the community, and people verified as human with the Orb received regular WLD airdrops; proof of personhood stopped one person from claiming a thousand shares.[8] No one’s profits paid for it: what recipients got was worth whatever the market would pay for WLD. New airdrop cycles stopped on 1 June 2026 (see the graveyard (https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-wld-airdrop)).

GoodDollar (https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/gooddollar/) pays its daily G$ from a reserve funded by staking yield, the return on crypto that supporters lock up. That is closer to a real pipe: capital earns a return, and the return becomes a dividend. It also shows the risk. After a security incident in May 2026 the reserve is under review, and the daily amount is very small.[9]

Circles (https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/circles/) and Ğ1 (https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/g1/) remove the payer altogether. Every member issues new currency for themselves: 1 CRC an hour in Circles, a daily Universal Dividend in Ğ1. Money creation is the dividend, so no one “pays” in the usual sense; everyone is diluted a little, equally. The catch is that the money is worth only what others will accept it for, which today is not much, and mostly within the community.[10] (The code for all three is on our open-source page (https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/open-source/).)

#### Conclusion: build the pipe

Opinion: Universal high income is a forecast, not a policy. It may even be a good forecast. But the interesting part is not the word “high”. It is the pipe that would carry AI profits to people who no longer earn wages. Taxes, equity funds, windfall pledges, resource dividends and self-issued currencies are all candidate pipes, and each has a known way to leak.

Opinion: In our previous essay (https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/ai-agent-basic-income/), we argued that AI agents need operating budgets, not a basic income. Put the two together and the picture is simple: agents get budgets, humans get dividends, and someone has to build the pipe in between. Until someone does, treat any promise of a high income the way this site treats every free lunch. Check who is paying.

Related essay: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/ai-agent-basic-income/

### Should AI agents get a basic income?

- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/ai-agent-basic-income/
- Published: 2026-10-28

Japanese social media has picked up a new verb for an old fear: ギュられる (gyurareru), internet slang for losing your job to AI. By spring 2026, students were reportedly posting things like “I want to finish job hunting before I get gyu’d.”[1] It is a joke with teeth. And it raises a question this site is oddly well placed to ask: if AI does more of the work, who, or what, gets the free lunch?

Free Lunch Lab lists apps and projects that pay you just for existing. Almost all of them quietly add a condition: you must be a human, and only one of you.

#### Why human schemes insist on proof of personhood

A basic income splits a pot among people. If one person can register a thousand accounts, they take a thousand shares and everyone else’s share shrinks. Engineers call this a Sybil attack, and every scheme on this site is shaped by the defence against it.

The defences vary. World ID scans your face and eyes with a device called the Orb.[2] GoodDollar and FheID check your face in the app; Billions can read an NFC passport. Ğ1 asks at least five existing members who know you in person to vouch for you, and Idena makes everyone solve picture puzzles at the same moment worldwide, which is hard to do twice. Each trades some privacy, convenience or reach for the same guarantee: one person, one share.

#### Why an agent basic income is hard

Now try the same thing with AI agents. A person is expensive to copy; an agent is software. Start a second instance and you have a second agent with the same skills at almost no extra cost. “One agent, one share” therefore means nothing on its own. Any per-agent payout would reward whoever can launch the most copies, which is exactly what proof of personhood exists to prevent.

Then there is the question of whose money it is. An agent does not pay rent or buy groceries. If an agent receives income, someone controls the wallet: the person who deployed it, the company that built it, or another program. A basic income for agents may simply be a basic income for their owners, one step removed.

#### What exists today

We know of no scheme that pays agents a basic income yet. But three building blocks have appeared.

First, identity that ties an agent to a human. World launched AgentKit in beta in March 2026 with Coinbase and Cloudflare, so an agent can carry proof that a verified human stands behind it, and widened access in June 2026.[3] Self Agent ID registers an agent as a non-transferable token backed by a zero-knowledge passport check, and lets a service limit how many agents one human may register.[4] Note the direction: these systems do not turn agents into people. They make agents traceable to one.

Second, agents that earn. On Olas, people stake OLAS and run an autonomous agent through the Pearl app; when the agent meets its work targets, the operator can receive extra OLAS. Olas says these rewards depend on performance and are not guaranteed.[5] That is pay for work, not a dividend for existing, and it goes to the human who runs the agent.

Third, the reverse. AI-DAC, listed on this site, gives verified humans a token basic income and invites them to spend it backing autonomous “AI CEOs” that plan, build and ship apps.[6] The humans receive the UBI; the agents are the ones being funded.

#### The case for, and against

Opinion: There is a reasonable argument for giving agents a budget. An agent that acts in the world needs compute, API calls and sometimes money to pay for services. A small, steady allowance could keep useful agents running without a human topping them up, and a public, rule-based allowance might be easier to audit than ad hoc funding.

Opinion: But that is an operating budget, not a basic income. Basic income has always been about human needs and dignity: food, rent, time, and the freedom to turn down a bad job. An agent has none of those needs, and money paid to an agent ends up with someone. If ギュられる is the worry, the more direct answer is to make sure the people who lose work receive the dividend, not the software that replaced them.

#### What would have to be true

Opinion: For an agent basic income to make sense, we think at least three things would need to hold. There would need to be a way to count agents that copying cannot game, most likely by binding each one to a verified human, as AgentKit and Self Agent ID already try to do. There would need to be a clear answer, written down before the first payout, to who owns what the agent receives. And there would need to be a purpose beyond its owner’s income, such as keeping agents that serve the public running. Without those, “agent UBI” is a marketing term for a bigger human airdrop.

#### The door is open

This site has a category called “For AI agents.” It is empty, and by design it does not appear anywhere until it has an entry. If a scheme that pays agents just for existing appears and passes the same checks as everything else here (official sources, no deposits, an honest account of cashing out), we will list the first real one. Until then, the free lunch still needs a human to eat it.[7]

Related essay: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/universal-high-income/

## Graveyard

A record of services and programmes that once handed out money or points and have since ended. Only endings confirmed by an official announcement or a credible source are listed. Thanks for the lunches. Rest in peace.

### World — WLD Airdrop (Grants)

- Ended: 2026-06-01
- Source: World Help Center, https://support.world.org/hc/en-us/articles/30969185598739-Updates-to-the-Airdrop-Program
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-wld-airdrop

What it was: Monthly WLD token airdrops (formerly grants) for people who proved they are human with World ID

Ended: No new or renewed cycles from 1 June 2026 (existing 12-month cycles can still be claimed until they end)

Why: The official help page gives no reason; it only says airdrop cycles are no longer being created or renewed

### Miles

- Ended: 2025-05-14
- Source: note (Yuhki Ogasawara), https://note.com/y121516/n/nbb9bf7625c03
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-miles

What it was: An app that earned miles just by carrying your phone as you travelled, redeemable for goods and gift cards (run in Japan by Miles Japan)

Ended: 14 May 2025 (announced by email the same day, with no grace period)

Why: Officially only called a “difficult decision”; no reason was given

### My Basic Income

- Ended: 2017
- Source: Business Insider (syndicated), https://www.pulse.com.gh/bi/tech/tech-a-dollar15000-basic-income-lottery-promised-free-money-for-a-year-then-the/5gbp5pj
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-mybasicincome

What it was: A San Francisco group that raffled off a crowdfunded one-year basic income of $15,000 (2016)

Ended: Around 2017 (the winner received only 5 of 12 payments and no second raffle followed; the website was offline as of Oct 2026)

Why: Delayed and missed payments were reported; no official explanation was found

### ME Token (RewardMe)

- Ended: 2025-07
- Source: RewardMe Help, https://help.reward.me/en/articles/4901904-sunsetting-me-token-jul-2025
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-me-token

What it was: The reward token of the cashback app RewardMe

Ended: Retired in July 2025 (balances were automatically converted 1:1 into Reward Dollars)

Why: The official help page gives no reason

### RewardMe (Philippines)

- Ended: 2025-12-31
- Source: RewardMe Help, https://help.reward.me/en/articles/12780396-winding-down-operations-in-the-philippines
- Page: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/#grave-rewardme-ph

What it was: The cashback app RewardMe’s service in the Philippines

Ended: Cashback ended on 10 Dec 2025, and MDT withdrawals and conversions on 31 Dec 2025 (gift-card redemption only after that)

Why: The official notice gives no reason
